preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '0')
preconditions.description: All non-empty lines (excluding the terminating '0') are valid test cases, each starting with an integer n followed by a permutation of integers 1 to n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(n) <= 100000 for n in [line.split()[0] for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '0'])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first integer n satisfies 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == int(n) + 1 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '0' for n in [line.split()[0]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the permutation line contains exactly n integers (1-based index).

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= int(x) <= int(n) for x in line.split()[1:]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '0' for n in [line.split()[0]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the permutation contains integers between 1 and n, inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(line.split()[1:])) == int(n) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '0' for n in [line.split()[0]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the permutation contains each integer from 1 to n exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout.strip() in ['ambiguous', 'not ambiguous'] for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '0')
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'ambiguous' or 'not ambiguous'.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda p: p == [p[i-1] for i in p])(list(map(int, line.split()[1:])))) == (stdout.strip() == 'ambiguous') for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '0'
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is 'ambiguous' if and only if the permutation is equal to its inverse permutation. The inverse permutation is defined as the list where the i-th element (1-based) is the position of integer i in the original permutation.
